summary:
A poster on panel `i` spreads until it hits a strictly shorter panel on each side. So its width is the gap
between the nearest shorter panel on the left and the nearest shorter panel on the right. A monotonic stack
finds the nearest shorter panel for every position in one pass per side: O(n).

question.md:
For every panel, imagine a poster exactly as tall as that panel. It must cover the panel and may extend sideways
over neighbouring panels, but only ones at least as tall. How wide can it get?

- **Equal heights don't stop it**, only strictly shorter panels do.
- **The answer is one width per panel**, in order.
- **Up to 10⁵ panels.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Equal neighbours: a poster can spread over panels of the **same** height.
- The shortest panel reaches the whole fence.
- "No shorter panel on a side" means the poster reaches that end (index −1 or n as the boundary).

think.md:
**How far can a bar reach?** For bar `i` with height `h`, the widest stretch where every bar is at least `h` runs from
just after the **nearest shorter bar on the left** to just before the **nearest shorter bar on the right**. Both
"nearest shorter" positions come from a monotonic stack in one pass each: pop bars that are not shorter than the
current one; what's left on top is the nearest shorter bar.

**Why this finds the best rectangle.** Any rectangle under a histogram is limited by its lowest bar. Taking each bar as
the lowest and stretching as far as possible covers the best rectangle for that height, so the best of these is the
best overall.

approaches.title: Spread each poster panel by panel

idea.md: For each panel, walk left and right while neighbours are at least as tall.

lines.text: Spread left over panels at least as tall.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** (e.g. all panels equal). **Space O(1)** besides the output.

steps.text: Panel 0 (height 3): spreads over panels 0..2, stopped by the left end and panel 3. Width 3.
Panel 1 (height 5): spreads over panels 1..1, stopped by panel 0 and panel 2. Width 1.
Panel 2 (height 4): spreads over panels 1..2, stopped by panel 0 and panel 3. Width 2.
Panel 3 (height 1): spreads over panels 0..6, stopped by the left end and the right end. Width 7.
Panel 4 (height 4): spreads over panels 4..5, stopped by panel 3 and panel 6. Width 2.
Panel 5 (height 6): spreads over panels 5..5, stopped by panel 4 and panel 6. Width 1.
Panel 6 (height 2): spreads over panels 4..6, stopped by panel 3 and the right end. Width 3.

walk.title: For each panel, spread the poster left and right while the neighbouring panels are at least as tall.

limits.md: Walks overlap heavily. The nearest shorter panel on each side, found with stacks, gives every width directly.

approaches.title: Nearest shorter panel, from both sides

idea.md:
Left pass: a stack of panel indices; pop while the top is at least as tall as the current panel; the
remaining top is the nearest shorter panel on the left (−1 if none). Right pass: the same from the right
(n if none). Width = `right − left − 1`.

lines.text: Nearest shorter panel on each side, defaulting to the ends (−1 and `n`).
Left to right: after popping, the top of the stack is the nearest strictly shorter panel to the left. Then `i` joins the stack.
A panel at least as tall as panel `i` can never be the nearest shorter panel for anything further right: `i` is closer and no taller. Discard it for good.
The mirror pass from the right gives the nearest strictly shorter panel on the right.
The poster fills the open gap between the two stoppers: `right − left − 1` panels.

notes.java: The width is filled in during the right pass, once both stoppers are known.
notes.cpp: The width is filled in during the right pass, once both stoppers are known.
notes.c: The width is filled in during the right pass, once both stoppers are known.

steps.text: Left pass, panel 0 (3): pop nothing (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: none (−1).
Left pass, panel 1 (5): pop nothing (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: 0.
Left pass, panel 2 (4): pop panels [1] (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: 0.
Left pass, panel 3 (1): pop panels [2, 0] (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: none (−1).
Left pass, panel 4 (4): pop nothing (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: 3.
Left pass, panel 5 (6): pop nothing (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: 4.
Left pass, panel 6 (2): pop panels [5, 4] (not shorter). Nearest shorter on the left: 3.
Right pass, panel 6 (2): pop nothing. Nearest shorter on the right: none (7). Width 7 − 3 − 1 = 3.
Right pass, panel 5 (6): pop nothing. Nearest shorter on the right: 6. Width 6 − 4 − 1 = 1.
Right pass, panel 4 (4): pop panels [5]. Nearest shorter on the right: 6. Width 6 − 3 − 1 = 2.
Right pass, panel 3 (1): pop panels [4, 6]. Nearest shorter on the right: none (7). Width 7 − -1 − 1 = 7.
Right pass, panel 2 (4): pop nothing. Nearest shorter on the right: 3. Width 3 − 0 − 1 = 2.
Right pass, panel 1 (5): pop nothing. Nearest shorter on the right: 2. Width 2 − 0 − 1 = 1.
Right pass, panel 0 (3): pop panels [1, 2]. Nearest shorter on the right: 3. Width 3 − -1 − 1 = 3.

walk.title: Two monotonic-stack passes: the nearest shorter panel on the left, then on the right. The poster fills the gap between them.

takeaways.md:
- **Reach of each bar = nearest shorter on both sides**, via two monotonic-stack passes.
- Boundaries −1 and n stand for "no shorter bar".
- **Pitfall:** popping only strictly taller bars (stops at equal ones, undercounting the width).
